text:
anya: heads-up — after flipping attention-optimizer-v2 on the canary pool last night I see a clear tail reg. p50 is fine (~22ms) but p95 ~45ms and p99 spikes to ~310ms for long sequences (seq_len=1024). baseline (v1) doesn't show the spike. rolling v2 back removed it.

kevin: ugh. do we have a quick reproducer? microbench or only live traces?

anya: short reproducer attached — microbench with sequence sweep reproduces tail but only under mixed batch sizes. command I used:

```
./tools/bench_harness --model /models/gpt-small --kernels attention-optimizer-v2 --seq-lens 16,128,512,1024 --batch-distribution "[1:0.2,4:0.7,16:0.1]" --samples 5000 --log tail
```

logs snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T22:11:03Z] sample=4114 seq=1024 batch=4 latency=312ms stack="kv_cache_wait -> fused_attn_wait -> kernel_swap"
[2026-03-18T22:11:03Z] sample=4119 seq=1024 batch=1 latency=305ms stack="kv_cache_wait -> kernel_select_serial"
```

sam: can you dump the telemetry bucket labels? need to see if it's one pod or spread across many. also confirm if it's only with kv-cache enabled.

anya: telemetry shows the majority of p99s coming from 3 hosts (host-07, host-12, host-18). kv-cache=true for those requests. when I re-ran with kv-cache disabled the p99 drops back close to baseline.

nishit: interesting — optimizer-v2 introduced an async kernel swap path intended to reduce cold kernel loads. could be higher contention for cache locks when kv-cache is hot. might be a coordination bug.

kevin: hypothesis checklist: 1) kernel-swap lock contention; 2) batching interleaving causing head-of-line blocking; 3) different code path for batch-size=1 vs >1; 4) quantization codepath mismatch. we should triage in that order.

rachel: agree. add a deterministic run with single sequence length and single batch size to rule out interleaving. if the spike disappears, it's the mixed-batch interaction.

anya: did that: single seq=1024 batch=4 stable; single seq=512 batch=1 stable. mixed batch dist reproduces. so points to interleaving.

kevin: ok that's narrowing it. can someone run the kernel profiler on host-07 while reproducing? want to see syscalls, kernel schedule stalls, and futex wait times.

anya: profiling job started on host-07: `perf record -F 99 -g -- ./bench_harness ...` will attach results in ~20m.

ci-bot: build 2026.03.18-527 passed: attention-optimizer-v2 artifact available at s3://redwood-artifacts/attn-opt/v2/2026-03-18-527.tar.gz

sam: also add a microbench variant that randomizes batch offsets to emulate prefix diversity; we should rule out pathological queue ordering in the serving runtime.

nishit: quick code pointer — in v2 the kernel selection now tries speculative swapping: it preloads an alternate kernel if estimated next seq_len > current. that logic assumes stable request ordering. if mixed batches interleave, speculative swaps may thrash.

kevin: excellent find. test: disable speculative swap flag and re-run mixed-batch reproducer. if tail disappears we have root cause.

anya: ran with `--no-spec-swap` and p99 dropped to 48ms (close to baseline). leaving repro running to collect more samples.

rachel: if that fixes it, plan: 1) revert speculative swap on canary and prod, 2) open a follow-up RFC to redesign speculative policy to be request-order aware, 3) add unit/integration tests for mixed-batch interleaving. owners?

kevin: i'll own RFC (I'll draft by EOD), rachel you ok to handle canary rollback and prod gating?

rachel: yep I'll rollback canary in the next deploy window and create a rollout gate.

anya: created an internal issue: INF-3141 documenting reproducer, perf trace, and initial findings. attaching perf flame and raw bench CSV.

sam: short-term mitigation idea: add a cheap heuristic: only spec-swap when a run-length of same seq_len >= N (N=4) observed on that worker. avoids thrash without major perf hit.

nishit: that heuristic sounds reasonable. we'll need telemetry to measure false positives/negatives. add a flag so we can A/B test on one host pool.

ci-bot: deploy job queued for rollback to attention-optimizer-v1 on canary at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z.

anya: action items summary: 
- rachel: rollback canary + gate prod (due 2026-03-19 02:00Z)
- kevin: RFC draft for speculative-swap redesign (due EOD)
- nishit: prototype heuristic AND add flag for A/B test (due 2 days)
- sam: extend bench harness with randomized batch-offset mode + add unit test for swap logic (due 2 days)
- anya: attach perf traces and bench CSVs to INF-3141 (done)

rachel: noted. I'll also add a short customer-facing blurb in #incidents if we see any impact.

kevin: once RFC is up we'll schedule a small design sync. thanks all for quick triage. :thumbsup: 

anya: will keep thread updated with perf artifacts and canary status. closing when rollback confirmed stable.
